## Excursions via Riobamba: Baños waterfalls or Chimborazo and Ingapirca

[Riobamba](/ecuador/place/riobamba/) is a city in Ecuador's central Andes that works well as **the link between two different excursion days**. One route arrives after visiting the waterfalls near Baños. The other leaves Riobamba, crossing the Chimborazo highlands towards the archaeological complex of Ingapirca and Cuenca.

Read the Riobamba excursion catalogue carefully: the city's presence on both routes does not mean both journeys start here and return to the same hotel. Choose based on the sequence of transfers and your booked overnight stays.

## Baños and the Waterfall Route: arriving in Riobamba

On the [Baños: Waterfall Route and Swing at the End of the World excursion](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/), the main stops are in **Baños** and the Pastaza River valley. The itinerary includes Agoyán, Bridal Veil and Devil's Cauldron waterfalls, canyon views and the swing at Casa del Árbol. A **transfer to Riobamba taking around 2 hours** follows.

The full excursion day, including transfers, takes **8–9 hours**. Guiding is in Russian. A canopy ride above Pastaza Canyon costs **an additional $15 per person** and is optional, not a compulsory part of the programme.

This day suits travellers who want to see green gorges, waterfalls and panoramas, then continue to the central Andes by evening. **Riobamba is the end point of this day**, not the departure point for Baños.

## Chimborazo and Ingapirca: from Riobamba to Cuenca

The [Chimborazo and Ingapirca excursion](/ecuador/chimborazo-reserve/chimborazo-and-ingapirca/) has a different route: **Riobamba → Chimborazo Reserve → Ingapirca → Cuenca**. In the nature section, visitors discover high-altitude landscapes and observe vicuñas; in the historical section, they explore the heritage of the Cañari and Inca peoples.

The programme specifies **11–12 hours including travel**, Russian-speaking guiding and elevations of approximately **3750–4800 m**. This outing is much colder and higher than the waterfalls near Baños. Even a short walk by a mountain refuge at this altitude can feel unfamiliar.

Access to the interior areas of Ingapirca depends on opening hours. Under this programme's conditions, visits on Mondays and Tuesdays are from the outside; check actual access for your date because the site's schedule can change.

## Choosing between the two routes

| Route | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Baños → Riobamba | Waterfalls, canyon and transfer |
| Riobamba → Cuenca | Chimborazo and Inca ruins |

For the waterfall day, take lightweight rain protection and non-slip footwear. The Chimborazo route requires warm layers, protection from wind and sun, and attention to acclimatisation. **These routes are not interchangeable in terms of physical demands or travel time**.

When you take the two days in sequence, Riobamba provides a natural overnight stop between the green slopes of Baños and Chimborazo's dry highlands. Do not assume that the reverse order or a same-day return to the starting point is possible without changing the overall itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions via Riobamba

### Which excursions are connected with Riobamba?

We offer a [route through Baños and the waterfalls](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) arriving in the city and a separate [Chimborazo and Ingapirca excursion](/ecuador/chimborazo-reserve/chimborazo-and-ingapirca/) departing from Riobamba.

### Can we see everything in one day?

The excursions are lengthy in their own right: **8–9 hours** and **11–12 hours** respectively, including transfers. Combining them into one day would require a separately agreed itinerary.

### Where is it higher and colder?

On the **Chimborazo** section, at elevations of up to approximately **4800 m**. Warm clothes and acclimatisation are especially important.

### Which route is better for history and which for nature?

For archaeology, choose **Ingapirca** together with Chimborazo. For waterfalls and the Pastaza Valley, take the **Baños** route.

## Santa Cruz highlands excursions: tortoises, lava tunnels and lunch

The interior of [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) in the Galápagos is markedly different from its dry coastal areas. **Giant land tortoises** inhabit the green highlands, and lava tunnels remain in the volcanic rock. Ada Tours offers two separate excursion products in this part of the island, with different inclusions.

The key question is whether you want **a route with lunch included** or also wish to explore **lava tunnels**. Visiting the same tortoise habitat does not make the products identical.

## Santa Cruz highlands: tortoises and lunch

The [Santa Cruz Highlands: Tortoises and Lunch excursion](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-tortoises-lunch/) explicitly includes **a guided visit to the highlands and lunch**. It is a group programme with **English-speaking guiding**.

On the related tour, the visit is scheduled **on the day of arrival in the Galápagos**, on the way from Baltra Airport to the hotel on Santa Cruz. After lunch, the itinerary includes hotel check-in and a visit to the dive centre. That does not make scuba diving part of the highlands excursion.

This format is convenient for an initial introduction to the island's nature, when you want to see tortoises, have lunch and continue to your accommodation. The meal is confirmed as included, although the menu, exact venue and alternative meal arrangements are not specified.

## Giant tortoises and lava tunnels

The second product, [Santa Cruz: Giant Tortoises and Lava Tunnels](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-lava-tunnels/), combines tortoise watching, local birds and visiting volcanic tunnels. It is a **group excursion with English-speaking guiding**.

Lava tunnels formed when the surface of flowing lava cooled faster than the molten material beneath it: lava continued moving and left cavities behind. Erosion and collapses have subsequently changed some sections. Visiting the tunnels therefore requires attention to uneven ground and lighting, and actual access depends on trail conditions.

A separate lunch **is not listed as included in this excursion**, so it cannot automatically be transferred from the neighbouring product. On the related tour the visit is part of the programme, but no separate standalone price is specified.

## Watching tortoises without disturbing them

Tortoises move freely across the island and sometimes appear close to roads; the local conservation service monitors animals in these locations. When you encounter them, keep your distance, avoid blocking their path, do not feed them and follow the guide's instructions. You cannot guarantee their behaviour or the opportunity for close-up photographs.

The highlands may be wetter and cooler than the coast. Wear closed shoes with reliable soles and light rain protection, and leave time for a leisurely walk. If you have limited mobility, check trail surfaces and whether descending into a tunnel is required.

## Frequently asked questions about the Santa Cruz highlands

### Which excursion includes lunch?

The [Tortoises and Lunch programme](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-tortoises-lunch/) explicitly includes lunch.

### Which excursion includes lava tunnels?

The [Tortoises and Lava Tunnels programme](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-lava-tunnels/). Its route differs from the lunch option.

### What language is used for guiding?

Both programmes provide **English-speaking guiding**.

### Can we be guaranteed to see a tortoise?

Giant tortoises inhabit the highlands, but they are **wild animals**. Their exact location and behaviour depend on natural conditions.

### Can we visit the highlands on arrival day?

Yes. On one of our tours, this is planned en route from Baltra to the hotel. The timing must be coordinated with the actual flight and transfer.

## Santa Cruz highlands: giant tortoises and lunch after arrival

The interior of [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) differs from its dry coast: green pastures, humid areas and trails provide opportunities to see giant land tortoises. After flying to the Galápagos, this is one of the most direct ways to start discovering the archipelago's terrestrial wildlife.

Our group programme takes place **on the way from Baltra Airport to the hotel on Santa Cruz**. It includes **a guided highlands visit and lunch**. Guiding is **in English**; a separate duration and standalone price are not specified for this excursion.

## Why tortoises inhabit the highlands

Galápagos giant tortoises are large terrestrial herbivores. In the highland regions of Santa Cruz, they move between pastures and areas of denser vegetation. During a walk, you may observe a tortoise moving slowly, lifting its head, choosing grass or resting.

This is an encounter with wildlife on land, not a demonstration involving an animal held by an instructor. Tortoises choose where to move; at different times there may be more or fewer of them. A particular number of animals at any site cannot be promised.

The [Santa Cruz highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) are also interesting for their contrast with the coast. Changes in elevation bring changes in humidity and vegetation: after a hot shoreline, travellers enter a greener landscape.

## How the excursion works on arrival day

This stop is included **on the first day in the Galápagos**. After arriving via Baltra, the group travels to Santa Cruz, visits the highlands with a guide, observes tortoises and has lunch.

Travellers then continue to Hotel Fiesta. The day's tour programme also includes meeting the dive-centre staff and trying on or checking equipment. This is **the next part of a specific tour**, not a mandatory service on the separate tortoise excursion. Its presence on the full itinerary does not mean that diving, equipment rental or diving lessons are included in this excursion.

This sequence divides a busy arrival day into manageable stages: travel and first encounters with island wildlife, followed by checking in and preparing for the rest of the programme.

## How to behave near tortoises

The main rule is to watch without disturbing the animals. Do not touch their shells, sit too close for a photograph, feed them or block their way. The guide will show where to stop and what distance to maintain.

Closed shoes and light clothing with a rain jacket are suitable for the walk: the highlands are wetter and have different weather from the coast. Bring water, sun protection and be ready for a short walk on natural ground.

Conserving giant tortoises is an important part of the work of the [Galápagos National Park and conservation organisations](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Seeing animals in their habitat helps visitors appreciate why local rules and leaving no litter are important.

## Highlands or a marine excursion: which to choose?

The tortoise programme works particularly well **on arrival day**, when travel from the airport to the hotel is already planned. It does not require another sea crossing and introduces wildlife in its land habitat.

For a different experience, compare it with a [boat excursion to Bartolomé](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/bartolome-island-boat-tour/), with volcanic views and possible snorkelling, or a [trip to Isabela](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/isabela-island-speedboat-tour/), focused on lagoons and lava islets beside the water. Other options appear in the [Galápagos excursions catalogue](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/).

A diving itinerary can combine several such experiences, but **this standalone excursion is about land tortoises and lunch**. Marine diving is not automatically part of it.

## Frequently asked questions about the Santa Cruz highlands

### Where does the excursion take place?

In the green interior of Santa Cruz Island. The stop is scheduled **on the way from Baltra Airport to the hotel**.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. Lunch in the highlands is included along with the nature visit and guiding.

### What language is used?

**English** is specified for this group programme.

### Are giant tortoises guaranteed to be seen?

The highlands are their natural habitat, but their exact number and location vary. Watching them depends on conditions in the wild.

### Is diving or equipment fitting included?

Diving is not included in the standalone excursion. Meeting the dive centre and checking equipment belong to the continuation of the day on the specific tour.

## Tours featuring the Santa Cruz giant tortoise excursion

The [Santa Cruz Highlands: Tortoises and Lunch excursion](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-tortoises-lunch/) takes place in the green interior of one of the Galápagos archipelago's main inhabited islands. Here, visitors observe giant land tortoises in their natural habitat, discover island vegetation and see how the landscape changes as the road climbs from the dry coast to the more humid highlands.

This page focuses on **multi-day itineraries that include this specific excursion module**. The wider journey matters as much as the tortoise visit: the day of arrival, later sea activities, accommodation and transfer arrangements all form part of the choice.

## Santa Cruz highlands on a four- or five-day diving trip

On [Galápagos Diving: 4 or 5 Days with Hotel Fiesta](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/), the highlands visit takes place **on the first day after arrival**. Travellers land on Baltra, then head for their accommodation on Santa Cruz. A guided highlands visit and lunch are included en route. After transferring to the hotel, the programme introduces the dive centre and checks equipment.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_ecuador_galapagos_diving_4_5_days}}

The main purpose of this multi-day journey is diving. The tortoise excursion therefore complements rather than replaces the marine section. The following day includes a check dive and other dives; specific dive sites are selected based on the day of the week, ocean conditions and participants' experience. **Consult the actual tour programme for the number of dives and additional services**, rather than inferring these from the name of the highlands excursion.

For travellers wanting to see terrestrial animals, this first day offers a distinct nature experience before heading out to sea. For divers, it also serves a practical purpose: after the flight, they can discover the island and prepare for their upcoming dives.

## Why tortoises are observed in the highlands

The [Santa Cruz highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) are known for humid vegetation, pastures and natural areas where giant tortoises move according to conditions. Giant land tortoises are among the symbols of the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), but sightings at a precise distance or in a predetermined number cannot be guaranteed because these are free-ranging animals.

Observation takes place without feeding or touching them. The Galápagos National Park Directorate requires visitors to keep **at least 2 m from animals**, stay on authorised trails and refrain from taking natural objects. For photographs, stop quietly and use your camera's zoom rather than approaching a tortoise for a close-up.

Vegetation here is markedly different from the volcanic landscape around [Baltra Airport](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/). Even a brief stop along the road gives a sense of the archipelago's ecological variety. However, the highlands excursion is not a visit to every island and does not automatically include the research station, marine beaches or additional protected areas.

## Combining arrival, excursion and hotel

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Arrival | Baltra Airport |
| Transfer | Travel to Santa Cruz Island |
| Highlands | Guided tortoise watching and lunch |
| After excursion | Hotel Fiesta and dive centre |
| Next day | Beginning of marine dives |

Our excursion includes **guiding and lunch**. Air tickets, transfers, rental of a complete equipment set and diving-package terms belong to the specific multi-day tour. Check them separately before purchasing.

Santa Cruz can have brief showers, soft ground and damp trail sections. For walking, wear closed non-slip shoes and bring water and light rain protection. Photograph tortoises calmly, without rushing or making loud noises. On the first day, also consider how you feel after travelling.

## Who will enjoy this combination?

**Divers**, whose main reason for travelling is underwater exploration, can use the highlands visit to discover a land-based part of the archipelago's famous wildlife. **Nature lovers** should also consider the other side of the equation: the related multi-day tour specialises in diving and may have skill and health requirements. You can consider the standalone tortoise excursion independently of booking the entire diving programme.

If your main aim is peaceful animal watching without diving, compare [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and [Galápagos wildlife journeys](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/). Look at the actual island stops and number of land days: including the Galápagos on an itinerary does not mean it necessarily visits the Santa Cruz highlands.

Ada Tours can help coordinate inter-island transfers, accommodation and time for your preferred activities. The actual included services are determined by the selected programme; the number of dives, equipment rental and medical requirements do not belong to the tortoise excursion itself.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting the Santa Cruz highlands

### Is lunch included with the tortoise excursion?

Yes. Our standalone excursion includes **lunch in the highlands and a guided visit**. That does not mean all other meals are included in every tour.

### Will we see giant tortoises?

The Santa Cruz highlands are a place to observe giant land tortoises in their natural environment. The timing and number of sightings depend on the animals and visiting conditions. Do not approach too closely, touch or feed them.

### Do we have to go diving to join the excursion?

The [tortoise excursion](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-tortoises-lunch/) itself takes place on land and requires no diving. However, the linked [multi-day tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) focuses on diving; suitability for its other days needs to be assessed separately.

## Excursions on and from Santa Cruz Island: tortoises or nearby islands?

[Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) is a convenient starting point for discovering the Galápagos and travelling to nearby islands. We offer **excursions with different formats**: a transfer from Baltra to Puerto Ayora through the highlands, outings to tortoises and lava tunnels, and sea trips to **Floreana** and **South Plaza**.

Before choosing, distinguish an excursion **on Santa Cruz itself** from a journey **departing Santa Cruz for another island**. They are not interchangeable simply because they use the same accommodation base.

## Santa Cruz: meeting the tortoises after arrival

The [Santa Cruz Island: Giant Tortoises and Lava Tunnels excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/santa-cruz-island-tour/) begins after arrival on Baltra. It includes crossing the Itabaca Channel, travelling through the Santa Cruz highlands, watching giant tortoises and walking through part of the lava tunnels.

The itinerary lasts **6 hours** and includes guiding **in English or Spanish**, **transfers and lunch**. The National Park entry fee and Galápagos transit-control card are listed separately under exclusions. Include them **in addition to the excursion price** when comparing the full cost.

Another option is the [group highlands excursion with tortoises and lava tunnels](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-lava-tunnels/). Its focus is the island's natural environment; included services and duration differ from the standalone six-hour product, and lunch is not listed as included.

## Floreana: a marine excursion and island history

The [Floreana Island excursion from Santa Cruz](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/floreana-island-tour-from-santa-cruz/) begins around Puerto Ayora and takes visitors to a different island. Here, nature observations combine with the history of seafarers and early Galápagos settlers.

We offer a **6-hour itinerary** with **English- or Spanish-speaking guiding, transfer and lunch** confirmed. The description mentions possible encounters with sea turtles, blue-footed boobies and other animals; sightings of a particular species cannot be guaranteed.

Choose Floreana if you want to experience **a new island landscape**, rather than another walk through the familiar Santa Cruz highlands.

## South Plaza: sea lions, iguanas and a shore walk

The [South Plaza Island excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/) also departs from Santa Cruz. The journey includes approximately **1.5 hours aboard a yacht** to the island, followed by a walk near sea lion colonies, land iguanas and birds.

The programme lasts **6 hours**, including **English- or Spanish-speaking guiding, transfers and lunch**. The island park fee and transit card, by contrast, are listed separately. This is **a sea day with an island walk**, not a visit to lava tunnels.

## Planning days and costs

| Travel goal | Suitable excursion |
|---|---|
| Tortoises and lava tunnels | Santa Cruz |
| History and wildlife | Floreana |
| Sea lions and iguanas | South Plaza |

Marine excursions require time for boarding and sailing. Their order depends on weather, national-park requirements and available places aboard the vessel. Galápagos wildlife is protected: do not approach animals for photographs and follow the guide's route.

**Prices and inclusions differ from product to product.** Do not assume that lunch, tickets, guiding language or duration of one excursion apply to another. On a longer archipelago stay, leave some flexibility between sea days for weather-related changes.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions departing Santa Cruz

### Can I visit Floreana and South Plaza on one day?

These are **two separate excursions**, each lasting six hours. Combining both on a single day is not confirmed in the current programmes.

### Where can I see giant tortoises?

In the [Santa Cruz highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/), visited by the relevant nature excursions.

### Which excursion works on arrival day?

For arrivals via Baltra, the [Santa Cruz itinerary with an Itabaca Channel crossing](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/santa-cruz-island-tour/) is designed for that purpose. Its timing is coordinated with the flight.

### Are park tickets included in the price of every excursion?

No. Some standalone Ada Tours excursions **list the National Park entry fee and transit card as exclusions**. Read the individual product's terms.

### Can I choose a Russian-speaking guide?

The marine products listed confirm **English and Spanish**. Russian is not listed as included and needs a separate arrangement.
